title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-noah-patel
content:
Purpose:
Quick debugging notes and breadcrumb trail for the tensor/checkpoint load failures observed when serving the new 30B variant. Work-in-progress; this is effectively a scratchpad for commands tried, observed errors, hypotheses, and next steps.

Context / symptom:
- Endpoint start fails during model init on dedicated pool (p4d). Logs show failure at weights load stage.
- Failure happens intermittently across nodes; sometimes node gets farther (loads one or two shards) then fails.
- Affects both torch checkpoint (.bin) and safetensors variants (we tried both).

Files involved (from artifacts bucket):
- s3://redwood-checkpoints/30b-v2/index.json
- s3://redwood-checkpoints/30b-v2/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin
- ...-00008-of-00008.bin
- s3://redwood-checkpoints/30b-v2/pytorch_model.safetensors (we also generated a combined safetensors in some runs)

What I tried (chronological):
1) Basic sanity: aws s3 ls / aws s3 cp
- aws s3 ls s3://redwood-checkpoints/30b-v2 --recursive  --> all 9 files present
- aws s3 cp s3://redwood-checkpoints/30b-v2/pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin ./  (downloaded)
- md5sum mismatch observed on one download: local md5 != expected-md5 (index.json contains checksums)
  * Suspected transient network causing truncated file.

2) Retried with --no-progress and increased retries:
- aws s3 cp --no-progress --only-show-errors --no-verify-ssl --quiet ... 
- Also tried aws s3 cp with --expected-size not available; used awscli default retry (did not fully fix).

3) Switched to aws s3 sync and aria2c for parallel segmented downloads:
- aria2c -x16 "https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-checkpoints/.../pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin"
- Result: faster, but still occasional checksum mismatch for shard 00003 (file size off by 4096 bytes).

4) Verified on a different network (local laptop vs cloud VM) — same behavior on cloud instances; laptop downloads fine. Hypothesis: S3 transfer issues in particular AZ?

5) Tried huggingface-cli snapshot-download (we mirrored to HF hub for testing):
- huggingface-cli snapshot-download --repo-id redwood/30b-v2 --revision main --cache-dir ./hfcache
- Result: download completed and HF reports correct checksums. But serving job still fails when loading HF-cached files directly.

6) Attempted to load locally on a node (python REPL):
- torch.load('pytorch_model-00001-of-00008.bin', map_location='cpu')
  -> ValueError: unexpected EOF while reading bytes (raised for shard 00003)
- safetensors.load_file('pytorch_model.safetensors')
  -> RuntimeError: safetensors: malformed file (header inconsistent) on combined safetensors file built by conversion script

7) Tried incremental/staged loading in codebase (served loader):
- Loader uses streaming-based merge of shards. When shard read fails, loader doesn't retry and aborts.
- Observed log: "Failed to memory-map shard /srv/model/pytorch_model-00003-of-00008.bin: Unexpected end of file"

Observed errors (snippets):
- "ValueError: Unexpected end of file while reading bytes" (Python/torch)
- "RuntimeError: Caught exception loading state_dict for Model: missing keys ..." (if partial)
- "safetensors: malformed file" (from safetensors lib)
- Low-level: "read() returned fewer bytes than expected" in our ingestion utility

Hypotheses so far:
- Hypothesis A: Network transfer intermittently truncates some shards when downloading in-parallel from S3 in given AZ. This yields corrupted shard files that pass a basic file existence check but fail on checksum/parse.
- Hypothesis B: Our conversion pipeline that created the combined safetensors may be buggy (we saw header inconsistency). The original sharded bin files are authoritative.
- Hypothesis C: Loader's streaming/merge logic (we map and then sequentially read shards into KV cache) has an off-by-one when computing expected file lengths for certain shards (leading to read() mismatch).
- Hypothesis D: Some nodes mount ephemeral disk with a bad sector/FS issue causing truncation when writing large files (~2GB each).

Investigations to validate/falsify:
- Re-download the problematic shard using different methods (curl, aws cli, s3fs, HF snapshot) and compare file sizes + sha256. --> Done: HF snapshot gives good shard. S3 direct sometimes bad.
- On a healthy download, compute sha256 and compare against index.json captured checksums. Need to extend index.json to include sha256 (we currently have md5).
- Try serving from HF cached copy (which had correct checksums) to see if loader still trips. If serving still fails, it's loader logic, not file.
- Try loading the same file in a local python process on the node to rule out disk/memory at runtime. (Torch load succeeded on HF-cached file locally).
- Re-run downloads but write to tmpfs (ramdisk) to test disk corruption hypothesis. If writing to tmpfs fixes it, likely disk issue.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Added pre-start checksum validation in startup script: after download, compute sha256 and abort start if mismatch. This prevents corrupted artifacts from making it into runtime, but doesn't fix why downloads are corrupted.
- Implemented simple retry loop that re-downloads shard up to 3x on checksum mismatch. Reduced incidents but didn't eliminate them.

Relevant code pointers:
- serving-runtime/loader/checkpoint_loader.py (streaming merge logic)
- infra/s3-sync/scripts/download-checkpoint.sh (awscp wrapper used by deploy)
- tools/checksum/compute_checksums.py (script to compute md5, needs sha256)

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run a controlled experiment: spawn VM in same AZ as failing host, download all shards sequentially with single threaded aws cp, compute sha256, and compare with HF snapshot. Capture network logs (tcpdump) if mismatch persists.
- [ ] Make index.json include sha256 checksums. Will need to re-run upload pipeline (PR pending: GH-PR-578).
- [ ] Add integrity checks during tar/untar or any conversion step. Our safetensors conversion job should validate resulting file (and we should keep original shards).
- [ ] Audit nodes' ephemeral disks (dmesg) for I/O errors; coordinate with infra to check underlying volumes in the busy AZ.
- [ ] Hardening: change our loader to do per-shard checksum verification and to retry reads (and fall back to alternative mirror e.g., HF).

Notes about loader memory behavior:
- Some failures only show up when using GPU loader path (we map shards directly into GPU memory); suspected OOM-like behavior (but error message not explicit). Add additional logging around torch.cuda.memory_allocated at load time.

Confidence levels:
- A & B: medium. Evidence points to corrupted shards from S3/transfer OR a conversion bug. HF snapshot working suggests original artifacts are ok; S3 copies sometimes get corrupted.
- C & D: low->medium. Need to rule out with tmpfs test and per-node disk checks.

Immediate next steps (short):
- Run tmpfs download test on failing AZ and post results into ticket JIRA-INF-892. (Assigned to me).
- Push index.json sha256 PR (GH-PR-578) and add start-time checksum verifier.
- Instrument loader for per-shard checksum + retry + fallback to HF mirror.

If anything else occurs while I'm away, ping @maya / @olivia and reference this file.

End of scratchpad.
